<section class="chapter wrap" id="ch5"><div class="ch-head"><span class="plate">5</span><div><p class="eyebrow">Chapter 5 · Commands</p><h2>Get ready</h2></div></div><div class="story"><span class="tag">The story so far</span><p>The environment is installed and the code is built. Some preparations remain.</p><p>Do the cards in sequence. You do card 5.1 each time. You do the other cards one time.</p></div><div class="goals"><b>After this chapter you can</b><ul><li>Start a session with three commands.</li><li>Save your work in Git.</li><li>Have the nuScenes mini data in the correct folder.</li></ul></div><div class="cards"><article class="card solo" id="c5-1"><header class="card-h"><span class="cid">5.1</span><h3>Start each session</h3><span class="slides">Each time</span><label class="got" for="got-c5-1"><input type="checkbox" id="got-c5-1" data-got="c5-1"> Got it</label></header><div class="card-b"><div class="prose">
<p>Do this each time you open a new terminal. A <b>terminal</b> is a window where you type commands.</p>
<div class="cmd"><div class="cmd-h"><span>Terminal</span><button type="button" class="copy">Copy</button></div><pre>cd ~/Workspace/Work_V/bevfusion
conda activate bevfusion
export BEVFUSION_LOW_MEM=1</pre></div><ol class="steps"><li>Line 1 goes to the project folder.</li><li>Line 2 starts the Python environment of this project.</li><li>Line 3 decreases the memory that camera models use.</li></ol><div class="box trap"><span class="tag">Trap</span><p>If you see <code>No module named 'torch'</code> or <code>torchpack: command not found</code>, you did not do line 2.</p></div><p class="oneline">Three commands, each time.</p></div></div></article>
<article class="card solo" id="c5-2"><header class="card-h"><span class="cid">5.2</span><h3>Make a safe copy of the code</h3><span class="slides">One time</span><label class="got" for="got-c5-2"><input type="checkbox" id="got-c5-2" data-got="c5-2"> Got it</label></header><div class="card-b"><div class="prose">
<p>Git keeps old versions of the code. These commands make a branch with the name <code>my-work</code>. They save the repairs that we made for your graphics card.</p>
<div class="cmd"><div class="cmd-h"><span>Terminal</span><button type="button" class="copy">Copy</button></div><pre>git switch -c my-work
git add mmdet3d
git commit -m &quot;Repairs for GTX 1650&quot;</pre></div><div class="box exam"><span class="tag">Caution</span><p>Do not use <code>git add .</code> in this project. It also adds the large files in <code>pretrained/</code>.</p></div><div class="box analogy"><span class="tag">Analogy</span><p>A commit is a saved game for code. If you break something, you go back.</p></div><p class="oneline">Save the repairs before you change anything.</p></div></div></article>
<article class="card" id="c5-3"><header class="card-h"><span class="cid">5.3</span><h3>Stop half-precision numbers</h3><span class="slides">One time</span><label class="got" for="got-c5-3"><input type="checkbox" id="got-c5-3" data-got="c5-3"> Got it</label></header><div class="card-b"><div class="prose">
<p>The project uses short numbers (<b>fp16</b>) to save memory. Your graphics card calculates them incorrectly. This command stops fp16:</p>
<div class="cmd"><div class="cmd-h"><span>Terminal</span><button type="button" class="copy">Copy</button></div><pre>sed -i &#x27;/^fp16:/,/growth_interval/c\fp16: null&#x27; configs/default.yaml
grep fp16 configs/default.yaml</pre></div><p>The second command must show <code>fp16: null</code>.</p><div class="box note"><span class="tag">From our tests on your computer</span><p class="hand">25 % of the results were not valid</p><p>We calculated the same layer with short and with normal numbers on your GTX 1650. With short numbers, one quarter of the results was <code>NaN</code> (not a number).</p></div><div class="box trap"><span class="tag">Trap</span><p>If you forget this, you see <code>matrix contains invalid numeric entries</code>.</p></div><p class="oneline">No fp16 on this graphics card.</p></div><div class="shots"><figure class="codeshot"><pre>fp16:
  loss_scale: 
    growth_interval: 2000</pre><figcaption>configs/default.yaml · before</figcaption></figure><figure class="codeshot"><pre>fp16: null</pre><figcaption>configs/default.yaml · after</figcaption></figure></div></div></article>
<article class="card solo" id="c5-4"><header class="card-h"><span class="cid">5.4</span><h3>Add swap, and repair the draw program</h3><span class="slides">One time</span><label class="got" for="got-c5-4"><input type="checkbox" id="got-c5-4" data-got="c5-4"> Got it</label></header><div class="card-b"><div class="prose">
<p>Your computer has 7.6 GB of memory and no swap. <b>Swap</b> is disk space that the computer uses when the memory is full.</p>
<div class="cmd"><div class="cmd-h"><span>Terminal</span><button type="button" class="copy">Copy</button></div><pre>sudo fallocate -l 8G /swapfile
sudo chmod 600 /swapfile
sudo mkswap /swapfile
sudo swapon /swapfile
free -h</pre></div><p>The line <code>Swap</code> must show 8 GB. After a restart, do <code>sudo swapon /swapfile</code> again.</p><p>The draw program uses a name that does not exist. This command corrects it:</p><div class="cmd"><div class="cmd-h"><span>Terminal</span><button type="button" class="copy">Copy</button></div><pre>sed -i &#x27;s/from torchpack.utils.tqdm import tqdm/from tqdm import tqdm/&#x27; tools/visualize.py</pre></div><div class="box note"><span class="tag">From our tests on your computer</span><p class="hand">Linux stopped one test</p><p>Without swap, the memory was full when we drew the boxes of the model. Exit code 137.</p></div><p class="oneline">Swap prevents "Killed". The repair makes visualize.py start.</p></div></div></article>
<article class="card" id="c5-5"><header class="card-h"><span class="cid">5.5</span><h3>Get the data</h3><span class="slides">One time · nuscenes.org</span><label class="got" for="got-c5-5"><input type="checkbox" id="got-c5-5" data-got="c5-5"> Got it</label></header><div class="card-b"><div class="prose">
<p><b>nuScenes</b> is a set of drives with photos, LiDAR points and correct boxes. Use the <b>mini</b> version. It has 10 drives and is approximately 4 GB.</p>
<ol class="steps"><li>Go to <a href="https://www.nuscenes.org">nuscenes.org</a> and make an account.</li><li>Download "Mini" (<code>v1.0-mini.tgz</code>).</li><li>Put the files in the project:</li></ol><div class="cmd"><div class="cmd-h"><span>Terminal</span><button type="button" class="copy">Copy</button></div><pre>mkdir -p data/nuscenes
tar -xzf ~/Downloads/v1.0-mini.tgz -C data/nuscenes
ls data/nuscenes</pre></div><p>The last command must show <code>maps</code>, <code>samples</code>, <code>sweeps</code> and <code>v1.0-mini</code>.</p><div class="box exam"><span class="tag">Security</span><p>Download only from nuscenes.org. Do not use copies from other websites.</p></div><p class="oneline">Download mini, unpack it into data/nuscenes.</p></div><div class="shots"><figure class="codeshot"><pre>data/nuscenes/
├── maps/
├── samples/    photos and points
├── sweeps/     data in between
└── v1.0-mini/  the lists</pre><figcaption>What you must see</figcaption></figure></div></div></article>
<article class="card solo" id="c5-6"><header class="card-h"><span class="cid">5.6</span><h3>Make the list of examples</h3><span class="slides">One time</span><label class="got" for="got-c5-6"><input type="checkbox" id="got-c5-6" data-got="c5-6"> Got it</label></header><div class="card-b"><div class="prose">
<p>The data program writes file names that the recipes do not read. These commands make links between the names. Do them one time only.</p>
<div class="cmd"><div class="cmd-h"><span>Terminal</span><button type="button" class="copy">Copy</button></div><pre>ln -s data/nuscenes nuscenes
ln -s nuscenes_infos_train_radar.pkl data/nuscenes/nuscenes_infos_train.pkl
ln -s nuscenes_infos_val_radar.pkl data/nuscenes/nuscenes_infos_val.pkl</pre></div><p>Now make the list of examples:</p><div class="cmd"><div class="cmd-h"><span>Terminal</span><button type="button" class="copy">Copy</button></div><pre>python tools/create_data.py nuscenes \
  --root-path ./data/nuscenes --out-dir ./data/nuscenes \
  --extra-tag nuscenes --version v1.0-mini</pre></div><p>At the end, you must see lines such as <code>load … car database infos</code>.</p><div class="box trap"><span class="tag">Trap</span><p>If you see <code>No such file … nuscenes_infos_train.pkl</code>, the links are missing.</p></div><p class="oneline">Links first, then create_data.py.</p></div></div></article>
</div><div class="quiz" id="quiz5"><div class="quiz-h"><h3>Checkpoint 5: Get ready</h3><span class="score"></span></div><div class="q" data-a="b"><p>Which command do you do in each new terminal?</p><div class="opts jsonly"><button type="button" data-k="a">sudo swapon /swapfile</button><button type="button" data-k="b">conda activate bevfusion</button><button type="button" data-k="c">git switch -c my-work</button></div><p class="why" hidden>It starts the Python environment.</p><div class="nojs nq"><label class="w"><input type="radio" name="q19"> <span>sudo swapon /swapfile</span></label><label class="r"><input type="radio" name="q19"> <span>conda activate bevfusion</span></label><label class="w"><input type="radio" name="q19"> <span>git switch -c my-work</span></label><p class="why2">It starts the Python environment.</p></div></div><div class="q" data-a="b"><p>Why do you stop fp16?</p><div class="opts jsonly"><button type="button" data-k="a">It needs an account</button><button type="button" data-k="b">This graphics card calculates it incorrectly</button><button type="button" data-k="c">It is too slow</button></div><p class="why" hidden>In our test, 25 % of the results were NaN.</p><div class="nojs nq"><label class="w"><input type="radio" name="q20"> <span>It needs an account</span></label><label class="r"><input type="radio" name="q20"> <span>This graphics card calculates it incorrectly</span></label><label class="w"><input type="radio" name="q20"> <span>It is too slow</span></label><p class="why2">In our test, 25 % of the results were NaN.</p></div></div><div class="q" data-a="a"><p>You see <code>Killed</code>. What is full?</p><div class="opts jsonly"><button type="button" data-k="a">The memory of the computer</button><button type="button" data-k="b">The disk</button><button type="button" data-k="c">The graphics card</button></div><p class="why" hidden>Close programs or add swap. A full graphics card shows "CUDA out of memory".</p><div class="nojs nq"><label class="r"><input type="radio" name="q21"> <span>The memory of the computer</span></label><label class="w"><input type="radio" name="q21"> <span>The disk</span></label><label class="w"><input type="radio" name="q21"> <span>The graphics card</span></label><p class="why2">Close programs or add swap. A full graphics card shows "CUDA out of memory".</p></div></div></div></section>
<section class="chapter wrap" id="ch6"><div class="ch-head"><span class="plate">6</span><div><p class="eyebrow">Chapter 6 · Commands</p><h2>Train, test and draw</h2></div></div><div class="story"><span class="tag">The story so far</span><p>The data is ready. Now you train your first model.</p><p>It is the small LiDAR model, because it fits on your graphics card. Then you test the full model of the authors.</p></div><div class="goals"><b>After this chapter you can</b><ul><li>Start, stop and continue a training.</li><li>Read a line of the log.</li><li>Test a model and draw its boxes.</li></ul></div><div class="cards"><article class="card solo" id="c6-1"><header class="card-h"><span class="cid">6.1</span><h3>Train a model</h3><span class="slides">tools/train.py</span><label class="got" for="got-c6-1"><input type="checkbox" id="got-c6-1" data-got="c6-1"> Got it</label></header><div class="card-b"><div class="prose"><div class="box exam"><span class="tag">Caution</span><p>Close the browser and other large programs first. Training needs most of your memory.</p></div><p>This command trains the LiDAR model that fits on your card:</p><div class="cmd"><div class="cmd-h"><span>Terminal</span><button type="button" class="copy">Copy</button></div><pre>torchpack dist-run -np 1 python tools/train.py \
  configs/nuscenes/det/transfusion/secfpn/lidar/voxelnet.yaml \
  --run-dir runs/first \
  --data.samples_per_gpu 1 --data.workers_per_gpu 1 \
  --max_epochs 1</pre></div><div class="tbl"><table><tr><th>Part</th><th>Meaning</th></tr><tr><td><code>-np 1</code></td><td>Use 1 graphics card.</td></tr><tr><td><code>…voxelnet.yaml</code></td><td>The recipe.</td></tr><tr><td><code>--run-dir runs/first</code></td><td>Where the results go. Use a new name each time.</td></tr><tr><td><code>samples_per_gpu 1</code></td><td>Use 1 example in each step.</td></tr><tr><td><code>workers_per_gpu 1</code></td><td>Use 1 helper program to read data.</td></tr><tr><td><code>max_epochs 1</code></td><td>Do 1 pass.</td></tr></table></div><div class="box note"><span class="tag">From our tests on your computer</span><p class="hand">0.7 seconds for each step</p><p>Measured on your GTX 1650 with artificial examples. Real data can be different.</p></div><p class="oneline">One command: recipe, result folder, small batch.</p></div></div></article>
<article class="card solo" id="c6-2"><header class="card-h"><span class="cid">6.2</span><h3>Read the log</h3><span class="slides">runs/first/</span><label class="got" for="got-c6-2"><input type="checkbox" id="got-c6-2" data-got="c6-2"> Got it</label></header><div class="card-b"><div class="prose">
<p>The program writes one line from time to time. This is a real line from our test:</p>
<pre class="plain">Epoch [1][50/60]  lr: 1.066e-04, eta: 0:00:10, time: 0.686,
memory: 1440, loss/object/loss_heatmap: 1.5793, ...
loss: 6.0520, grad_norm: 10.9153</pre><div class="tbl"><table><tr><th>Word</th><th>Meaning</th></tr><tr><td><code>Epoch [1][50/60]</code></td><td>Pass 1, step 50 of 60.</td></tr><tr><td><code>lr</code></td><td>The learning rate now. <code>1.066e-04</code> = 0.0001066.</td></tr><tr><td><code>eta</code></td><td>The time that remains.</td></tr><tr><td><code>time</code></td><td>Seconds for one step.</td></tr><tr><td><code>memory</code></td><td>Memory on the graphics card, in MB.</td></tr><tr><td><code>loss</code></td><td>The total loss. <b>This number must decrease.</b></td></tr><tr><td><code>grad_norm</code></td><td>How large the gradient is.</td></tr></table></div><div class="wn"><div class="ok"><b class="h">Good</b><ul><li>the loss goes down, with small jumps</li></ul></div><div class="no"><b class="h">Stop and look</b><ul><li>the loss is <code>nan</code></li><li>the loss goes up for a long time</li></ul></div></div><div class="box note"><span class="tag">From our tests on your computer</span><p class="hand">Invalid box type: None</p><p>After a very short training, the test can stop with this message. The model found no objects in range. The checkpoint is safe. Continue the training.</p></div><p class="oneline">Look at one number first: loss.</p></div></div></article>
<article class="card solo" id="c6-3"><header class="card-h"><span class="cid">6.3</span><h3>Stop and continue</h3><span class="slides">tools/train.py</span><label class="got" for="got-c6-3"><input type="checkbox" id="got-c6-3" data-got="c6-3"> Got it</label></header><div class="card-b"><div class="prose">
<p>To stop a training, push <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd>. To continue for 1 more epoch:</p>
<div class="cmd"><div class="cmd-h"><span>Terminal</span><button type="button" class="copy">Copy</button></div><pre>torchpack dist-run -np 1 python tools/train.py \
  configs/nuscenes/det/transfusion/secfpn/lidar/voxelnet.yaml \
  --run-dir runs/second --resume_from runs/first/latest.pth \
  --data.samples_per_gpu 1 --data.workers_per_gpu 1 \
  --max_epochs 2</pre></div><div class="box key"><span class="tag">Key idea</span><p><code>--max_epochs 2</code> is the total. Epoch 1 is done, thus the program does epoch 2.</p></div><div class="box trap"><span class="tag">Trap</span><p>If you stop in the middle of an epoch, you lose that epoch. The program saves only at the end of an epoch.</p></div><p class="oneline">Continue from latest.pth, and write the total number of epochs.</p></div></div></article>
<article class="card solo" id="c6-4"><header class="card-h"><span class="cid">6.4</span><h3>What your computer can do</h3><span class="slides">GTX 1650 · 4 GB</span><label class="got" for="got-c6-4"><input type="checkbox" id="got-c6-4" data-got="c6-4"> Got it</label></header><div class="card-b"><div class="prose"><div class="tbl"><table><tr><th>Model</th><th>Test</th><th>Train</th></tr><tr><td>LiDAR small (<code>voxelnet.yaml</code>)</td><td><span class="yes">Yes</span></td><td><span class="yes">Yes</span></td></tr><tr><td>LiDAR large (<code>voxelnet_0p075.yaml</code>)</td><td><span class="yes">Yes</span></td><td><span class="nope">No, not enough memory</span></td></tr><tr><td>Camera and LiDAR (<code>convfuser.yaml</code>)</td><td><span class="yes">Yes, with low memory on</span></td><td><span class="nope">No, not enough memory</span></td></tr><tr><td>Camera only (<code>swint/default.yaml</code>)</td><td><span class="yes">Yes, with low memory on</span></td><td><span class="nope">No, the recipe has an error</span></td></tr><tr><td>PointPillars (<code>pointpillars.yaml</code>)</td><td>Not tested</td><td><span class="nope">No, the recipe has an error</span></td></tr></table></div><div class="box between"><span class="tag">Between the lines</span><p>Why can a model be tested but not trained? In training, the computer must keep all the numbers in the middle to calculate the gradient. This needs much more memory.</p></div><div class="box note"><span class="tag">From our tests on your computer</span><p class="hand">1.25 GB is always used</p><p>The CUDA software uses this memory before the model starts. Thus you have less than 3 GB.</p></div><p>To train the camera and LiDAR model, use a rented computer with a larger graphics card.</p><p class="oneline">Train the small LiDAR model. You can test the next three.</p></div></div></article>
<article class="card solo" id="c6-5"><header class="card-h"><span class="cid">6.5</span><h3>Test a model</h3><span class="slides">tools/test.py</span><label class="got" for="got-c6-5"><input type="checkbox" id="got-c6-5" data-got="c6-5"> Got it</label></header><div class="card-b"><div class="prose"><p>Test the full model of the authors:</p><div class="cmd"><div class="cmd-h"><span>Terminal</span><button type="button" class="copy">Copy</button></div><pre>torchpack dist-run -np 1 python tools/test.py \
  configs/nuscenes/det/transfusion/secfpn/camera+lidar/swint_v0p075/convfuser.yaml \
  pretrained/bevfusion-det.pth --eval bbox \
  --cfg-options data.workers_per_gpu=1</pre></div><p>Test your model:</p><div class="cmd"><div class="cmd-h"><span>Terminal</span><button type="button" class="copy">Copy</button></div><pre>torchpack dist-run -np 1 python tools/test.py \
  configs/nuscenes/det/transfusion/secfpn/lidar/voxelnet.yaml \
  runs/first/latest.pth --eval bbox \
  --cfg-options data.workers_per_gpu=1</pre></div><div class="box key"><span class="tag">Key idea</span><p>A test needs two things that agree: the recipe and the checkpoint. The recipe makes the empty model. The checkpoint fills it with numbers.</p></div><div class="box links"><span class="tag">Connects to</span><ul><li><a href="#c2-6">2.6</a> the scores mAP and NDS</li><li><a href="#c4-3">4.3</a> why this command uses --cfg-options</li></ul></div><p class="oneline">Recipe + checkpoint + --eval bbox = scores.</p></div></div></article>
<article class="card" id="c6-6"><header class="card-h"><span class="cid">6.6</span><h3>Draw the boxes</h3><span class="slides">tools/visualize.py</span><label class="got" for="got-c6-6"><input type="checkbox" id="got-c6-6" data-got="c6-6"> Got it</label></header><div class="card-b"><div class="prose"><p>Draw the correct boxes on the photos:</p><div class="cmd"><div class="cmd-h"><span>Terminal</span><button type="button" class="copy">Copy</button></div><pre>torchpack dist-run -np 1 python tools/visualize.py \
  configs/nuscenes/det/transfusion/secfpn/lidar/voxelnet.yaml \
  --mode gt --out-dir viz_gt --data.workers_per_gpu 1</pre></div><p>Draw the boxes that the model finds:</p><div class="cmd"><div class="cmd-h"><span>Terminal</span><button type="button" class="copy">Copy</button></div><pre>torchpack dist-run -np 1 python tools/visualize.py \
  configs/nuscenes/det/transfusion/secfpn/lidar/voxelnet_0p075.yaml \
  --mode pred --checkpoint pretrained/lidar-only-det.pth \
  --bbox-score 0.3 --out-dir viz_pred --data.workers_per_gpu 1</pre></div><div class="box exam"><span class="tag">Caution</span><p>The last command used all the memory in our test, and Linux stopped it. Add swap first (card 5.4). We did not do a test with swap.</p></div><div class="box key"><span class="tag">Key idea</span><p><code>gt</code> means ground truth, the correct answer. <code>pred</code> means prediction, the answer of the model. Compare the two.</p></div><p class="oneline">gt = correct boxes, pred = boxes of the model.</p></div><div class="shots"><figure class="shot" tabindex="0"><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Front photo with drawn boxes"><figcaption>This is how a drawing looks (demo video)</figcaption></figure></div></div></article>
</div><div class="quiz" id="quiz6"><div class="quiz-h"><h3>Checkpoint 6: Train, test and draw</h3><span class="score"></span></div><div class="q" data-a="b"><p>Which number must decrease in the log?</p><div class="opts jsonly"><button type="button" data-k="a">time</button><button type="button" data-k="b">loss</button><button type="button" data-k="c">memory</button></div><p class="why" hidden>The loss tells how bad the answers are.</p><div class="nojs nq"><label class="w"><input type="radio" name="q22"> <span>time</span></label><label class="r"><input type="radio" name="q22"> <span>loss</span></label><label class="w"><input type="radio" name="q22"> <span>memory</span></label><p class="why2">The loss tells how bad the answers are.</p></div></div><div class="q" data-a="b"><p>Epochs 1 to 3 are done. You want 2 more. What do you write?</p><div class="opts jsonly"><button type="button" data-k="a">--max_epochs 2</button><button type="button" data-k="b">--max_epochs 5</button><button type="button" data-k="c">--max_epochs 3</button></div><p class="why" hidden>The number is the total: 3 + 2 = 5.</p><div class="nojs nq"><label class="w"><input type="radio" name="q23"> <span>--max_epochs 2</span></label><label class="r"><input type="radio" name="q23"> <span>--max_epochs 5</span></label><label class="w"><input type="radio" name="q23"> <span>--max_epochs 3</span></label><p class="why2">The number is the total: 3 + 2 = 5.</p></div></div><div class="q" data-a="b"><p>Which model can you train on this computer?</p><div class="opts jsonly"><button type="button" data-k="a">convfuser.yaml</button><button type="button" data-k="b">voxelnet.yaml</button><button type="button" data-k="c">voxelnet_0p075.yaml</button></div><p class="why" hidden>Only the small LiDAR model fits.</p><div class="nojs nq"><label class="w"><input type="radio" name="q24"> <span>convfuser.yaml</span></label><label class="r"><input type="radio" name="q24"> <span>voxelnet.yaml</span></label><label class="w"><input type="radio" name="q24"> <span>voxelnet_0p075.yaml</span></label><p class="why2">Only the small LiDAR model fits.</p></div></div><div class="q" data-a="b"><p>What does <code>--mode gt</code> draw?</p><div class="opts jsonly"><button type="button" data-k="a">The boxes of the model</button><button type="button" data-k="b">The correct boxes</button><button type="button" data-k="c">The road</button></div><p class="why" hidden>gt means ground truth.</p><div class="nojs nq"><label class="w"><input type="radio" name="q25"> <span>The boxes of the model</span></label><label class="r"><input type="radio" name="q25"> <span>The correct boxes</span></label><label class="w"><input type="radio" name="q25"> <span>The road</span></label><p class="why2">gt means ground truth.</p></div></div></div></section>
<section class="chapter wrap" id="ch7"><div class="ch-head"><span class="plate">7</span><div><p class="eyebrow">Chapter 7 · Your own experiments</p><h2>Make changes</h2></div></div><div class="story"><span class="tag">The story so far</span><p>Now you are ready to change things.</p><p>There are four levels, from easy to difficult. Stay at one level until it is easy for you.</p></div><div class="goals"><b>After this chapter you can</b><ul><li>Make an experiment with one change.</li><li>Make your own recipe.</li><li>Cancel a change safely.</li></ul></div><div class="cards"><article class="card solo" id="c7-1"><header class="card-h"><span class="cid">7.1</span><h3>Level 1: change a value in the command</h3><span class="slides">Easy</span><label class="got" for="got-c7-1"><input type="checkbox" id="got-c7-1" data-got="c7-1"> Got it</label></header><div class="card-b"><div class="prose"><div class="box key need"><span class="tag">Key idea<span class="needtag">Remember this</span></span><p><mark class="need">Change one thing at a time. Then train and compare the scores. If you change two things, you do not know which one helped.</mark></p></div><p>Add these parts to the end of the training command. They are two changes, thus try them one at a time.</p><div class="cmd"><div class="cmd-h"><span>Terminal</span><button type="button" class="copy">Copy</button></div><pre>--optimizer.lr 0.00005</pre></div><div class="cmd"><div class="cmd-h"><span>Terminal</span><button type="button" class="copy">Copy</button></div><pre>--model.heads.object.num_proposals 100</pre></div><p>The first decreases the size of each change. The second lets the model find a maximum of 100 objects, not 200.</p><div class="box trap"><span class="tag">Trap</span><p>Use a new <code>--run-dir</code> for each experiment. If not, the new results mix with the old results.</p></div><p class="oneline">One change, new folder, compare.</p></div></div></article>
<article class="card" id="c7-2"><header class="card-h"><span class="cid">7.2</span><h3>Level 2: make your own recipe</h3><span class="slides">Easy</span><label class="got" for="got-c7-2"><input type="checkbox" id="got-c7-2" data-got="c7-2"> Got it</label></header><div class="card-b"><div class="prose"><div class="cmd"><div class="cmd-h"><span>Terminal</span><button type="button" class="copy">Copy</button></div><pre>cd configs/nuscenes/det/transfusion/secfpn/lidar
cp voxelnet.yaml my_model.yaml
cd -
code configs/nuscenes/det/transfusion/secfpn/lidar/my_model.yaml</pre></div><p>Find <code>max_voxels: [90000, 120000]</code>. Change the first number to <code>60000</code>. The model now uses a maximum of 60,000 boxes in training. Use <code>my_model.yaml</code> in the training command.</p><div class="box key"><span class="tag">Key idea</span><p>Put the file in the same folder. Then the program reads the same <code>default.yaml</code> files for it (card 4.3).</p></div><p class="oneline">Copy a recipe, change one line, use the new name.</p></div><div class="shots"><figure class="codeshot"><pre>voxelize:
  max_num_points: 10
  # before: [90000, 120000]
  max_voxels: [60000, 120000]</pre><figcaption>my_model.yaml · the change</figcaption></figure></div></div></article>
<article class="card solo" id="c7-3"><header class="card-h"><span class="cid">7.3</span><h3>Level 3: change the Python code</h3><span class="slides">Medium</span><label class="got" for="got-c7-3"><input type="checkbox" id="got-c7-3" data-got="c7-3"> Got it</label></header><div class="card-b"><div class="prose">
<p>Open <code>mmdet3d/models/fusion_models/bevfusion.py</code>. Find this line (line 337):</p>
<pre class="plain">        batch_size = x.shape[0]</pre><p>Add this line below it. Use the same number of spaces at the start.</p><div class="cmd"><div class="cmd-h"><span>Terminal</span><button type="button" class="copy">Copy</button></div><pre>        print(&quot;size of the map:&quot;, x.shape)</pre></div><p>Start a test. The program shows the size of the map for each example. You do not need to build Python code again.</p><div class="box formula"><span class="tag">What you must see</span><p>For the small LiDAR model you must see <code>torch.Size([1, 256, 128, 128])</code>.</p><p class="inwords">1 example, 256 features, 128 × 128 squares. Compare with card 3.3.</p></div><div class="box trap"><span class="tag">Trap</span><p>Python uses the spaces at the start of a line. A wrong number gives <code>IndentationError</code>.</p></div><p class="oneline">A print line is the best first change.</p></div></div></article>
<article class="card solo" id="c7-4"><header class="card-h"><span class="cid">7.4</span><h3>Level 4: change the C++ or CUDA code</h3><span class="slides">Difficult</span><label class="got" for="got-c7-4"><input type="checkbox" id="got-c7-4" data-got="c7-4"> Got it</label></header><div class="card-b"><div class="prose">
<p>Files that end with <code>.cpp</code>, <code>.cc</code> or <code>.cu</code> need a new build:</p>
<div class="cmd"><div class="cmd-h"><span>Terminal</span><button type="button" class="copy">Copy</button></div><pre>export CUDA_HOME=$CONDA_PREFIX TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=&quot;7.5&quot; MAX_JOBS=2
python setup.py develop</pre></div><div class="tbl"><table><tr><th>Part</th><th>Meaning</th></tr><tr><td><code>CUDA_HOME</code></td><td>Use the CUDA of this environment.</td></tr><tr><td><code>TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="7.5"</code></td><td>The type of your graphics card.</td></tr><tr><td><code>MAX_JOBS=2</code></td><td>Build 2 files at the same time, because your memory is small.</td></tr></table></div><p class="oneline">C++ and CUDA need a build. Python does not.</p></div></div></article>
<article class="card solo" id="c7-5"><header class="card-h"><span class="cid">7.5</span><h3>See and cancel your changes</h3><span class="slides">Git</span><label class="got" for="got-c7-5"><input type="checkbox" id="got-c7-5" data-got="c7-5"> Got it</label></header><div class="card-b"><div class="prose"><p>See what you changed:</p><div class="cmd"><div class="cmd-h"><span>Terminal</span><button type="button" class="copy">Copy</button></div><pre>git diff</pre></div><p>Cancel the changes in one file:</p><div class="cmd"><div class="cmd-h"><span>Terminal</span><button type="button" class="copy">Copy</button></div><pre>git restore mmdet3d/models/fusion_models/bevfusion.py</pre></div><div class="box exam"><span class="tag">Caution</span><p><code>git restore</code> deletes your changes in that file. Do card 5.2 first. If you do not, it can also delete the repairs for your graphics card.</p></div><p class="oneline">git diff shows, git restore cancels.</p></div></div></article>
<article class="card solo" id="c7-6"><header class="card-h"><span class="cid">7.6</span><h3>Your first week</h3><span class="slides">Plan</span><label class="got" for="got-c7-6"><input type="checkbox" id="got-c7-6" data-got="c7-6"> Got it</label></header><div class="card-b"><div class="prose"><ol class="steps"><li><b>Day 1.</b> Read chapters 1 to 3. Do the checkpoints.</li><li><b>Day 2.</b> Do cards 5.1 to 5.4. Start the download of the data.</li><li><b>Day 3.</b> Do cards 5.5 and 5.6. Draw the correct boxes (card 6.6). Look at the pictures.</li><li><b>Day 4.</b> Test the model of the authors (card 6.5). Write down mAP and NDS.</li><li><b>Day 5.</b> Train for 1 epoch (card 6.1). Watch the loss.</li><li><b>Day 6.</b> Make one level 1 change. Train again and compare.</li><li><b>Day 7.</b> Make the level 3 change. Read <code>forward_single</code> slowly.</li></ol><p class="oneline">One small thing each day.</p></div></div></article>
</div><div class="quiz" id="quiz7"><div class="quiz-h"><h3>Checkpoint 7: Make changes</h3><span class="score"></span></div><div class="q" data-a="c"><p>You change lr and max_voxels together. The score is better. <section class="block wrap" id="trouble"><h2>Problems and solutions</h2><p class="sub">Find the message that you see. The number tells you which card has the solution.</p><div class="tbl"><table><tr><th>Message</th><th>Solution</th></tr><tr><td><code>CUDA out of memory</code></td><td>The graphics card is full. Use the small model. Make sure that <code>samples_per_gpu</code> is 1 and <code>BEVFUSION_LOW_MEM</code> is 1. <a href="#c6-4">6.4</a></td></tr><tr><td><code>Killed, or exit code 137</code></td><td>The memory of the computer is full. Close programs. Add swap. <a href="#c5-4">5.4</a></td></tr><tr><td><code>matrix contains invalid numeric entries</code></td><td>fp16 is on. Stop it. <a href="#c5-3">5.3</a></td></tr><tr><td><code>No such file … nuscenes_infos_train.pkl</code></td><td>Make the links. <a href="#c5-6">5.6</a></td></tr><tr><td><code>No module named &#x27;torchpack.utils.tqdm&#x27;</code></td><td>Repair the draw program. <a href="#c5-4">5.4</a></td></tr><tr><td><code>No module named &#x27;torch&#x27;, or torchpack: command not found</code></td><td>Do <code>conda activate bevfusion</code>. <a href="#c5-1">5.1</a></td></tr><tr><td><code>min_lr_ratio</code></td><td>The camera recipe has an error. Use the small LiDAR model. <a href="#c6-4">6.4</a></td></tr><tr><td><code>Invalid box type: None</code></td><td>The model found no objects. Train more. <a href="#c6-2">6.2</a></td></tr></table></div></section>
<section class="block wrap" id="dict"><h2>Dictionary</h2><p class="sub">Each word has one meaning on this page.</p><dl class="dict"><div><dt>Augmentation</dt><dd>Small random changes to the examples in training.</dd></div><div><dt>Backbone</dt><dd>The first large part of a network. It finds features.</dd></div><div><dt>Batch</dt><dd>The examples in one step.</dd></div><div><dt>BEV</dt><dd>Bird's-eye view. The map from above.</dd></div><div><dt>Checkpoint</dt><dd>A file with saved parameters (<code>.pth</code>).</dd></div><div><dt>CUDA</dt><dd>Software that lets programs use an NVIDIA graphics card.</dd></div><div><dt>Epoch</dt><dd>One pass through all the examples.</dd></div><div><dt>Feature</dt><dd>A number that describes something. The model calculates it.</dd></div><div><dt>fp16</dt><dd>Short numbers that use less memory. Off on your computer.</dd></div><div><dt>Fusion</dt><dd>To put data from different sensors together.</dd></div><div><dt>GPU</dt><dd>The graphics card. It does many calculations at the same time.</dd></div><div><dt>Gradient</dt><dd>Tells how each parameter changes the loss.</dd></div><div><dt>Head</dt><dd>The last part of a network. It gives the answer.</dd></div><div><dt>Heatmap</dt><dd>A map that shows where an object probably is.</dd></div><div><dt>Learning rate (lr)</dt><dd>How large each change of a parameter is.</dd></div><div><dt>LiDAR</dt><dd>A laser sensor that measures distance.</dd></div><div><dt>Loss</dt><dd>A number that tells how bad the answer is.</dd></div><div><dt>mAP, NDS</dt><dd>The two test scores.</dd></div><div><dt>Neck</dt><dd>A part that joins features of different sizes.</dd></div><div><dt>Overfitting</dt><dd>The model learns the examples by heart.</dd></div><div><dt>Parameter</dt><dd>A number in the model that training changes.</dd></div><div><dt>Point cloud</dt><dd>Many LiDAR points together.</dd></div><div><dt>Sparse</dt><dd>Calculate only the full boxes.</dd></div><div><dt>Sweep</dt><dd>One full turn of the LiDAR.</dd></div><div><dt>Voxel</dt><dd>A small box in space.</dd></div></dl></section>
